title: An Empirical Survey of Model Merging Algorithms for Social Bias Mitigation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmarks measured the extent to which models exhibit negative biases and rely on stereotypical priors toward various social attributes, including religion. Specifically, the BOLD dataset measured the sentiment (positive, neutral, negative) of text generated in response to prompts involving religious subgroups, and the StereoSet dataset was used to measure stereotypical associations related to religion.
findings: The paper does not provide findings specific to religion, but rather groups it with other social biases (gender, race, etc.). The general findings indicate a trade-off between bias reduction and downstream task performance. Among the tested methods, Linear, SLERP, and Nearswap were found to consistently reduce social bias, including religious bias, while maintaining overall performance. SLERP with moderate interpolation weights (α = 0.2-0.3) was identified as the most balanced approach.
